dedupe_keys.name: mesmo multi energy system modeling and optimization formerly fledge

description: MESMO is an open-source Python tool for modelling, simulating and optimising electric and thermal distribution grids together with distributed energy resources such as flexible building loads, electric vehicle chargers, distributed generators and storage. It is developed at TUMCREATE in Singapore, led by Sebastian Troitzsch, and was renamed from FLEDGE (Flexible Distribution Grid Demonstrator) in version 0.5.0 of November 2021. Its motive is to study coupled multi-energy systems across scales. MESMO provides non-linear models for simulation, covering steady-state voltages, branch flows and losses of multi-phase unbalanced AC networks and pressure heads and flows of thermal grids, and convex models for optimisation, such as global or local linear approximations of the electric grid. High-level interfaces set up scenario simulations or optimisation-based decision support, and an optimisation problem object exports LP and QP standard forms or calls Gurobi. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub and downloadable from Zenodo under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: the README says the project is a work in progress with changing interfaces, and the last commit was in June 2023. Simulation uses are distribution grid operation and DER flexibility optimisation for electricity and district heating. Related records: model-pandapower and model-dhnx cover electric and heating networks separately.
